page: Amazon Web Services r8id.metal-48xl is a memory-optimized bare-metal server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Featuring 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, this x86_64 architecture platform includes a 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It also integrates 11400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the top tier for multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores both rank in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth tests, including both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached reads and writes, consistently achieve top-tier status. Additionally, the hardware features advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, which accelerate cryptography, vector calculations, and integer operations.

From a resource density perspective, the combination of high-capacity DDR5 memory, massive local NVMe SSD storage, and dedicated bare-metal CPU allocation offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead. The server excels in database operations, as demonstrated by top-tier Redis SET operations and PassMark database benchmark results. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, heavy data-processing pipelines, multi-threaded decompression, and medium-to-large scale LLM inference tasks.
